newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Westpac securitisation bond issue price.
newsitem.headline: Westpac securitisation bond issue price.

text.p: The Westpac Securitisation Trust's second public A$695 million four tranche bond issue announced last week has been priced, Westpac said on Tuesday.
The A$204 million of class A1 notes were priced at 12 basis points over the one month bank bill rate with an expected average life of 1.1 years.

The A$190 million of Class A2 notes were priced at 20 basis points over with an expected average life of 2.7 years and the A$287.1 million of Class A3 notes were priced at 24 basis points over with an expected average life of 6.1 years.
The A$13.9 million Class B notes were priced at 34 basis points with an expected average life of 6.1 years.
The expected weighted average life of the entire issue is 3.7 years.
The Class A notes are rated AAA/Aaa and the single Class B notes are rated AA minus.
The transaction, the WST Series 1997-3 issue, is Westpac's largest to date and takes the toal amount of home loan assets to A$2.289 billion.
Westpac said the issue was structured in four tranches to meet investor preferences.

"We are pleased to have priced an issue of this size within our market expectations in light of the number of recent issues of mortgage backed securities," said Kimberley Gire, Westpac's Head of Securisation.
"Now that the domestic programme is well established we will focus on diversifying our securitisation efforts through the recently announced offshore Eurobond programme," Gire said.

"Further issues into either market will be a function of pricing but ongoing support of both markets is an objective. This will allow us to continue to satisfy appetite for WST securities at levels that deliver value to both investors and our shareholders," she added in a statement.
